def.note: one byte; 0 is false, any non-zero byte is true; the writer emits 1 for true

CHUNK_SECTIONS.hand: a run of chunk sections read until the byte array ends: the count is the dimension's section count, which the packet's bytecode cannot say (ClientboundLevelChunkPacketData reads bytes; LevelChunk reads the sections out of them later)

ENTITY_DATA.hand: a loop terminated by a 0xff index byte whose entries dispatch on the serializer registry; the walker does not read a terminated loop with an equality test yet

def.note: No length prefix at all: read exactly ceil(bits/8) raw bytes, where `bits` is the node's own parameter (the schema emits it as a sibling of `t`). Bit i is bit (i mod 8) of byte i/8, counting from the least significant bit of each byte. In 26.2 the only size used is bits=20, i.e. exactly 3 bytes.
exactly `len` raw bytes, no count on the wire; `len` is the constant on the node, from the readBytes(n) call, so no member stands for it
four bytes, big-endian, signed two's complement
eight bytes, big-endian, signed two's complement

Read one unsigned byte b0. If b0 == 0 the value is (0,0,0) and NOTHING further is read. Otherwise read one unsigned byte b1 and a big-endian unsigned 32-bit integer u, and form the 48-bit value v = (u << 16) | (b1 << 8) | b0 (note this is mixed-endian on the wire: wire bytes are v[7:0], v[15:8], then u big-endian, i.e. v[47:40], v[39:32], v[31:24], v[23:16]). scale = b0 & 3; if (b0 & 4) != 0 then read a VarInt h and set scale |= ((h as unsigned 32-bit) << 2). Then x = q(v >> 3) * scale, y = q(v >> 18) * scale, z = q(v >> 33) * scale, where q(w) = min(w & 0x7FFF, 32766) * 2 / 32766 - 1. The components therefore occupy bits 3-17, 18-32 and 33-47 of v.
one tag in network form: a 1-byte tag id, then that tag's payload with no name; id 0 (TAG_End) is the whole value and carries no payload

0.name: TAG_End (EndTag)
0.payload: NO PAYLOAD — zero bytes follow the id byte. EndTag$1.load reads nothing from the DataInput: it charges accounter.accountBytes(8L) (an in-memory size charge, Tag.OBJECT_HEADER = 8, not a read) and returns EndTag.INSTANCE. Both skip overloads are a bare `return`, and EndTag.write(DataOutput) is a bare `return`, so nothing is consumed and nothing is produced. Id 0 occurs only as (a) the terminator of a compound, (b) the element type of an empty list, and (c) the 'absent NBT' marker at the top level of a nullable packet field.

1.name: TAG_Byte (ByteTag)
1.payload: Exactly 1 byte: a signed two's-complement 8-bit integer, range -128..127. Read with DataInput.readByte(). No prefix, nothing else.

2.name: TAG_Short (ShortTag)
2.payload: Exactly 2 bytes: a signed two's-complement 16-bit integer, BIG-ENDIAN (most significant byte first), range -32768..32767. Read with DataInput.readShort(): value = (b0 << 8) | b1, b0 read first.

3.name: TAG_Int (IntTag)
3.payload: Exactly 4 bytes: a signed two's-complement 32-bit integer, BIG-ENDIAN. Read with DataInput.readInt(). NOT a varint — fixed width, even though the surrounding packet format uses varints elsewhere.

4.name: TAG_Long (LongTag)
4.payload: Exactly 8 bytes: a signed two's-complement 64-bit integer, BIG-ENDIAN. Read with DataInput.readLong(). Fixed-width, not a varint.

5.name: TAG_Float (FloatTag)
5.payload: Exactly 4 bytes: an IEEE-754 single-precision (binary32) value, BIG-ENDIAN. Read with DataInput.readFloat() = Float.intBitsToFloat(readInt()) — read 4 bytes big-endian as a 32-bit pattern and reinterpret. NaN bit patterns pass through unchanged; do not normalise them.

6.name: TAG_Double (DoubleTag)
6.payload: Exactly 8 bytes: an IEEE-754 double-precision (binary64) value, BIG-ENDIAN. Read with DataInput.readDouble() = Double.longBitsToDouble(readLong()) — 8 bytes big-endian as a 64-bit pattern, reinterpreted.

7.name: TAG_Byte_Array (ByteArrayTag)
7.payload: A 4-byte BIG-ENDIAN signed 32-bit ELEMENT COUNT (DataInput.readInt), then exactly that many bytes — one signed 8-bit byte per element, read as a single block with DataInput.readFully(byte[]). Element width is 1, so the count is also the byte count; total payload = 4 + count. Count 0 = empty array, nothing follows. Negative count: there is NO explicit `count < 0` check (unlike TAG_List). A negative count flows into NbtAccounter.accountBytes(1L, count), which multiplies (1 * count, still negative) and calls accountBytes(long), whose first act is `if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException(...)`. So a negative count is rejected, but as an accounting error (an unchecked IllegalArgumentException), not a format check. A from-scratch decoder should simply treat count < 0 as malformed.

8.name: TAG_String (StringTag)
8.payload: A 2-byte UNSIGNED BIG-ENDIAN 16-bit length (0..65535) giving the number of BYTES that follow — not the number of characters — then exactly that many bytes of Java 'modified UTF-8' (CESU-8 with a two-byte NUL). Read with DataInput.readUTF(). Precisely: U+0001..U+007F occupy one byte; U+0000 and U+0080..U+07FF occupy two bytes (0xC0|c>>6, 0x80|c&0x3F) — an embedded NUL is 0xC0 0x80 and never 0x00; U+0800..U+FFFF occupy three bytes; a character above the BMP is encoded as its UTF-16 surrogate pair, each surrogate as its own three-byte sequence (6 bytes total), never as a 4-byte UTF-8 sequence. A plain UTF-8 decoder gets NUL and astral characters wrong. Maximum payload is 2 + 65535 bytes.

9.name: TAG_List (ListTag)
9.payload: Header then homogeneous elements: (1) ONE byte, signed, = the element tag id (DataInput.readByte); (2) FOUR bytes, BIG-ENDIAN signed 32-bit, = the element COUNT, not a byte length (DataInput.readInt); (3) exactly `count` elements, each the BARE PAYLOAD of the header's tag id — no per-element id byte, no per-element name. VALIDATION IN THE BYTECODE: count < 0 throws NbtFormatException (readListCount, `iflt`); element type 0 with count > 0 throws NbtFormatException('Missing type on ListTag'). EMPTY LIST: element type 0 with count 0 is legal and is exactly what the writer emits (ListTag.identifyRawElementType starts at 0 and returns 0 for an empty list), so a decoder must accept element type 0 whenever count is 0 and must not look up type 0 as a real element type. A non-zero element type with count 0 is also accepted. Nesting counts against the 512-level depth limit (load brackets loadList with pushDepth/popDepth).

10.name: TAG_Compound (CompoundTag)
10.payload: A sequence of named entries terminated by a zero byte. Loop: (1) read ONE byte, signed, with DataInput.readByte() — this is both the entry's tag id and the terminator; (2) if it is 0 (TAG_End) the compound ENDS IMMEDIATELY — the terminator is consumed and no name and no payload follow it; (3) otherwise read the entry NAME as a TAG_String payload, i.e. DataInput.readUTF(): a 2-byte unsigned big-endian BYTE length then that many bytes of modified UTF-8, exactly as for tag id 8. The name sits BETWEEN the id byte and the value and is present for every entry; (4) then read the entry VALUE as the bare payload of that tag id — no repeated id, no second name; (5) repeat from (1). Entries go into a java.util.HashMap, so ORDER IS NOT PRESERVED and a decoder must not rely on it; duplicate names are accepted on the wire and last-one-wins (Map.put). There is no entry count and no byte-length prefix — the terminator is the only end marker, so a compound cannot be skipped without walking it. Nesting counts against the 512-level depth limit.

11.name: TAG_Int_Array (IntArrayTag)
11.payload: A 4-byte BIG-ENDIAN signed 32-bit ELEMENT COUNT (DataInput.readInt), then exactly that many elements, each 4 bytes BIG-ENDIAN signed 32-bit (one DataInput.readInt per element). Total payload = 4 + 4*count. Count 0 = empty array. Negative count: no explicit check; it reaches NbtAccounter.accountBytes(4L, count), which yields a negative product and throws IllegalArgumentException. Treat count < 0 as malformed.

12.name: TAG_Long_Array (LongArrayTag)
12.payload: A 4-byte BIG-ENDIAN signed 32-bit ELEMENT COUNT (DataInput.readInt), then exactly that many elements, each 8 bytes BIG-ENDIAN signed 64-bit (one DataInput.readLong per element). Total payload = 4 + 8*count. The asymmetry is real and worth spelling out: the LENGTH is 32-bit while the ELEMENTS are 64-bit. Count 0 = empty array. Negative count: no explicit check; it reaches NbtAccounter.accountBytes(8L, count) and throws IllegalArgumentException. Treat count < 0 as malformed.

def.note: One var-int: 0 means absent; any other value n means present with the value n - 1. The writer emits (value + 1) when present and 0 when absent. This is NOT the schema's `optional` node, which is a boolean followed by the value.
